sections.overview: Pimelodus stewarti is a small long-whiskered catfish described from Brazil’s Tocantins River drainage.
sections.identification: It has gray flanks, a dark transverse band just before the dorsal fin, and a dark spot on the distal dorsal-fin rays. The reported maximum is 6.6 cm standard length.
sections.habitat: It is known from freshwater in the Tocantins drainage; detailed habitat preferences are not established in the sources consulted.
sections.diet: Species-specific feeding data are not given in the taxonomic description or summary consulted.
sections.behavior: The available account is chiefly taxonomic, and species-specific behavior remains poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not describe its reproductive biology.
sections.ecology: Its small size and Tocantins range set it apart from the other Pimelodus profiles here. P. pintado is a larger, densely spotted fish from the Laguna Merín basin. P. pohli comes from the São Francisco drainage and has a deeper body with rows of spots in smaller specimens. P. tetramerus occurs in the Tapajós–Tocantins region and has four dark flank bands.
sections.conservation: The current FishBase summary reports the global IUCN category Data Deficient, assessed in 2022; this means the available information is insufficient to determine risk.
